newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Australia seeks interest in gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Western Australia seeks interest in gas pipeline.

text.p: The Western Australia state government said on Thursday it will ask for expressions of interest from around the world as the next step in its sale of 1,540 kilometre Dampier-to-Bunbury Natural Gas Pipeline (DBNGP).
State energy minister Colin Barnett said parties could register their interest from Friday.
He said the sale of the pipeline, which carries a book value of over A$1 billion, could reap the highest price for a state-owned asset in Western Australia's history.
"The price at which it eventually sells will largely depend on its future earning potential, as determined by prospective bidders," Barnett said in a statement.
The pipeline was built in 1984 and is owned by the state through Alinta Gas.
The terms of the sale stipulate Alinta Gas and Western Power would retain priority rights on access to capacity needed to service residential and smaller customers.
The government would retain ownership of the pipeline easement and expand it from 30 metres to 100 metres to allow the new owner to expand capacity and to allow for additional pipelines.
Barnett said the pipeline sale was another step in the state's dergulation of the natural gas market.
"The sale process has been aggressive and will continue to be so in order to meet our target of completion by the end of this year," Barnett said.
"I am sure there will not be any shortage of parties interested in putting forward firm bids for the pipeline."
The pipeline transports gas from the North-West Shelf to residential and business consumers in the southwest corner of Western Australia.
Current capacity is 500 terajoules a day.

The North-West Shelf is an equal partnership between operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd, Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, Chevron Corp and the Royal Ducth/Shell group.
MiMi is a partnership between Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp.
